verdicts.reason: A keeps the original order (logo, can, headline, CTA) and groups the headline tightly with the CTA, but the legal line is unreadably tiny and the grey sticker placeholder sits awkwardly beside it at the bottom. B moves the headline above the can, which is acceptable, but the can shrinks and leaves big empty gaps above and below it. B's legal text is even smaller and its sticker is a cramped speck.

A's can is undersized and floats in loose, uneven gaps between the headline and the CTA, and its legal text and sticker are microscopic. B gives the can more presence and keeps a clearer stack, but the logo is shrunk and crammed right against the headline. B also leaves a dead gap between the can and the CTA, its legal text is illegible, and the sticker collides into the footer row.

A has a sensible top-to-bottom stack (logo, headline, can, CTA), though the can is small, the spacing is loose and the legal text is unreadably tiny. B pushes the can to the top edge and moves the brand logo into the middle of the canvas under it, which breaks the brand header and the reading order. B also leaves an empty band between the can and the logo and packs the headline, CTA, legal text and sticker into the bottom third.
